response.text:
## 1) Stationary/KKT condition

Let \(\widehat\Sigma=X^TX/n\), \(\xi=\xi^*\), and

\[
Q(u)=\frac12 u^T\widehat\Sigma u-u^T\xi+\lambda\|u\|_1 .
\]

Since \(Q\) is convex, \(\widehat u_\lambda\) is optimal iff

\[
0\in \widehat\Sigma \widehat u_\lambda-\xi+\lambda \partial \|\widehat u_\lambda\|_1 .
\]

Equivalently, there exists \(z\in\mathbb R^p\) such that

\[
\widehat\Sigma \widehat u_\lambda-\xi+\lambda z=0,
\]

where

\[
z_j=
\begin{cases}
\operatorname{sign}(\widehat u_{\lambda,j}), & \widehat u_{\lambda,j}\neq 0,\\
\in [-1,1], & \widehat u_{\lambda,j}=0.
\end{cases}
\]

Componentwise, the KKT conditions are

\[
(\widehat\Sigma \widehat u_\lambda-\xi)_j
=
-\lambda \operatorname{sign}(\widehat u_{\lambda,j})
\quad\text{if }\widehat u_{\lambda,j}\neq 0,
\]

and

\[
|(\widehat\Sigma \widehat u_\lambda-\xi)_j|\le \lambda
\quad\text{if }\widehat u_{\lambda,j}=0.
\]

---

## 2) Coordinate descent update

Fix all coordinates except the \(j\)-th. Write the current iterate as \(u^0\). Define

\[
a_j=\widehat\Sigma_{jj},
\]

and

\[
b_j=\xi_j-\sum_{k\neq j}\widehat\Sigma_{jk}u_k^0.
\]

As a function of \(v=u_j\), the objective becomes, up to constants independent of \(v\),

\[
q_j(v)=\frac12 a_jv^2-b_jv+\lambda |v|.
\]

Thus the coordinate update solves

\[
u_j^{\text{new}}
=
\arg\min_v\left\{\frac12 a_jv^2-b_jv+\lambda |v|\right\}.
\]

Using the soft-thresholding operator

\[
S(x,t)=\operatorname{sign}(x)(|x|-t)_+,
\]

the update is

\[
\boxed{
u_j^{\text{new}}
=
\frac{S(b_j,\lambda)}{a_j}
}
\]

or equivalently,

\[
\boxed{
u_j^{\text{new}}
=
S\left(
u_j^0-\frac{(\widehat\Sigma u^0-\xi)_j}{\widehat\Sigma_{jj}},
\frac{\lambda}{\widehat\Sigma_{jj}}
\right).
}
\]

A full coordinate descent iteration consists of cycling through \(j=1,\dots,p\).

---

## 3) Proximal gradient update

Split

\[
Q(u)=f(u)+\lambda \|u\|_1,
\]

where

\[
f(u)=\frac12 u^T\widehat\Sigma u-u^T\xi.
\]

Then

\[
\nabla f(u)=\widehat\Sigma u-\xi.
\]

Given current iterate \(u^0\) and step size \(\tau>0\), the proximal gradient update is

\[
u^{\text{new}}
=
\operatorname{prox}_{\tau\lambda\|\cdot\|_1}
\left(
u^0-\tau(\widehat\Sigma u^0-\xi)
\right).
\]

Because the proximal operator of the \(\ell_1\)-norm is soft-thresholding,

\[
\boxed{
u^{\text{new}}
=
S\left(
u^0-\tau(\widehat\Sigma u^0-\xi),
\tau\lambda
\right),
}
\]

componentwise,

\[
\boxed{
u_j^{\text{new}}
=
S\left(
u_j^0-\tau(\widehat\Sigma u^0-\xi)_j,
\tau\lambda
\right).
}
\]

For guaranteed monotone convergence, it is standard to take \(\tau\le 1/L\), where

\[
L=\lambda_{\max}(\widehat\Sigma).
\]

---

## 4) Coordinate descent implementation in R

The prompt as provided here refers to “the given R code” for generating the data and \(\xi^*\), but that code is not included in the message. Therefore the numerical iteration count and final vector cannot be uniquely reproduced here. The following code implements the required coordinate descent algorithm and will produce the requested numerical output when run with the supplied data-generating code.

The tuning parameter is

\[
\lambda=1.2\sqrt{\frac{\log p}{n}}
=
1.2\sqrt{\frac{\log 600}{600}}
\approx 0.123906.
\]

```r
soft <- function(x, t) {
  sign(x) * pmax(abs(x) - t, 0)
}

kkt_violation <- function(u, Shat, xi, lambda, zero.tol = 1e-8) {
  r <- as.vector(Shat %*% u - xi)

  nz <- abs(u) > zero.tol
  viol <- numeric(length(u))

  viol[nz] <- abs(r[nz] + lambda * sign(u[nz]))
  viol[!nz] <- pmax(abs(r[!nz]) - lambda, 0)

  list(
    max_violation = max(viol),
    active_size = sum(nz),
    worst_coordinate = which.max(viol),
    residual = r,
    component_violation = viol
  )
}

cd_lasso_precision <- function(Shat, xi, lambda,
                               tol = 1e-5,
                               maxit = 100000,
                               track = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)) {
  p <- length(xi)

  u <- numeric(p)
  grad <- -xi          # grad = Shat %*% u - xi, initially u = 0
  d <- diag(Shat)

  if (any(d <= 0)) stop("Some diagonal entries of Shat are nonpositive.")

  path <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = maxit + 1, ncol = length(track))
  colnames(path) <- paste0("j=", track)
  path[1, ] <- u[track]

  l1.change <- Inf

  for (iter in seq_len(maxit)) {
    u.old.sweep <- u

    for (j in seq_len(p)) {
      old <- u[j]

      # b_j = xi_j - sum_{k != j} Shat[j,k] u_k
      # using grad_j = Shat[j,] u - xi_j
      z <- d[j] * old - grad[j]

      new <- soft(z, lambda) / d[j]

      if (new != old) {
        delta <- new - old
        u[j] <- new
        grad <- grad + delta * Shat[, j]
      }
    }

    l1.change <- sum(abs(u - u.old.sweep))
    path[iter + 1, ] <- u[track]

    if (l1.change < tol) break
  }

  path <- path[seq_len(iter + 1), , drop = FALSE]

  list(
    u = u,
    iter = iter,
    l1.change = l1.change,
    path = path,
    kkt = kkt_violation(u, Shat, xi, lambda)
  )
}
```

Run the coordinate descent algorithm as follows.

```r

n <- 600
p <- 600
rho <- 0.3

# Use the supplied data-generating code here.

# X <- MASS::mvrnorm(n, rep(0, p), Sigma)
# Shat <- crossprod(X) / n
#
# xi <- xi.star  # whatever the supplied code defines as xi^*

lambda <- 1.2 * sqrt(log(p) / n)

fit_cd <- cd_lasso_precision(
  Shat = Shat,
  xi = xi,
  lambda = lambda,
  tol = 1e-5,
  track = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)
)

cat("Coordinate descent iterations:", fit_cd$iter, "\n")
cat("Final l1 change:", fit_cd$l1.change, "\n")

cat("Worst KKT coordinate:", fit_cd$kkt$worst_coordinate, "\n")
```

Plotting the tracked coordinates:

```r

  0:fit_cd$iter,
  fit_cd$path,
  type = "l",
  lty = 1,
  lwd = 2,
  col = 1:5,
  xlab = "Coordinate descent sweep",
  ylab = expression(hat(u)[j]),
  main = "Coordinate descent paths"
)

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = colnames(fit_cd$path),
  col = 1:5,
  lty = 1,
  lwd = 2,
  bty = "n"
)
```

```r
fit_cd$kkt$max_violation
```

is numerically close to zero. With the stopping rule \(\|u^{k+1}-u^k\|_1<10^{-5}\), one typically expects a small but nonzero KKT violation.

## 5) Proximal gradient implementation in R

```r
pg_lasso_precision <- function(Shat, xi, lambda, tau,
                               tol = 1e-5,
                               maxit = 1000000,
                               track = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)) {
  p <- length(xi)

  u <- numeric(p)

  path <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = maxit + 1, ncol = length(track))
  colnames(path) <- paste0("j=", track)
  path[1, ] <- u[track]

  l1.change <- Inf

  for (iter in seq_len(maxit)) {
    u.old <- u

    grad <- as.vector(Shat %*% u - xi)

    u <- soft(u - tau * grad, tau * lambda)

    l1.change <- sum(abs(u - u.old))
    path[iter + 1, ] <- u[track]

    if (l1.change < tol) break
  }

  path <- path[seq_len(iter + 1), , drop = FALSE]

  list(
    u = u,
    iter = iter,
    l1.change = l1.change,
    path = path,
    tau = tau,
    kkt = kkt_violation(u, Shat, xi, lambda)
  )
}
```

Run proximal gradient for the requested step sizes.

```r
taus <- c(0.01, 0.005, 0.001)

fits_pg <- vector("list", length(taus))
names(fits_pg) <- paste0("tau=", taus)

for (a in seq_along(taus)) {
  tau <- taus[a]

  fit <- pg_lasso_precision(
    Shat = Shat,
    xi = xi,
    lambda = lambda,
    tau = tau,
    tol = 1e-5,
    track = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)
  )

  fits_pg[[a]] <- fit

  cat("\nProximal gradient, tau =", tau, "\n")
  cat("Iterations:", fit$iter, "\n")
  cat("Final l1 change:", fit$l1.change, "\n")
  cat("First 10 components:\n")
  print(round(fit$u[1:10], 8))

  cat("KKT max violation:", fit$kkt$max_violation, "\n")
  cat("Active set size:", fit$kkt$active_size, "\n")
  cat("Worst KKT coordinate:", fit$kkt$worst_coordinate, "\n")
}
```

Plot the coordinate paths:

```r
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))

for (a in seq_along(taus)) {
  fit <- fits_pg[[a]]

  matplot(
    0:fit$iter,
    fit$path,
    type = "l",
    lty = 1,
    lwd = 2,
    col = 1:5,
    xlab = "Proximal gradient iteration",
    ylab = expression(hat(u)[j]),
    main = paste0("PG, tau = ", fit$tau)
  )

  legend(
    "topright",
    legend = colnames(fit$path),
    col = 1:5,
    lty = 1,
    lwd = 2,
    bty = "n"
  )
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

Optionally check that the step sizes are below \(1/L\):

```r
L <- max(eigen(Shat, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values)

cat("Lipschitz constant L =", L, "\n")
cat("1/L =", 1 / L, "\n")
cat("Requested step sizes:", taus, "\n")
```

The stationary condition is checked through

```r
fit$kkt$max_violation
```

for each proximal gradient fit. A small value confirms that the computed iterate satisfies the KKT conditions approximately. Note that stopping by

\[
\|u^{k+1}-u^k\|_1<10^{-5}
\]

does not directly impose the KKT condition, especially for small \(\tau\). A stricter stopping rule based on the KKT violation itself would be preferable if high stationarity accuracy is required.

```r
    path[iter + 1, ] <- u[track]

    if (l1.change < tol) break
  }

  path <- path[seq_len(iter + 1), , drop = FALSE]

  list(
    u = u,
    iter = iter,
    l1.change = l1.change,
    path = path,
    tau = tau,
    kkt = kkt_violation(u, Shat, xi, lambda)
  )
}
```

Run proximal gradient for the requested step sizes.

```r
taus <- c(0.01, 0.005, 0.001)

fits_pg <- vector("list", length(taus))
names(fits_pg) <- paste0("tau=", taus)

for (a in seq_along(taus)) {
  tau <- taus[a]

  fit <- pg_lasso_precision(
    Shat = Shat,
    xi = xi,
    lambda = lambda,
    tau = tau,
    tol = 1e-5,
    track = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)
  )

  fits_pg[[a]] <- fit

  cat("\nProximal gradient, tau =", tau, "\n")
  cat("Iterations:", fit$iter, "\n")
  cat("Final l1 change:", fit$l1.change, "\n")
  cat("First 10 components:\n")
  print(round(fit$u[1:10], 8))

  cat("KKT max violation:", fit$kkt$max_violation, "\n")
  cat("Active set size:", fit$kkt$active_size, "\n")
  cat("Worst KKT coordinate:", fit$kkt$worst_coordinate, "\n")
}
```

Plot the coordinate paths:

```r
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))

for (a in seq_along(taus)) {
  fit <- fits_pg[[a]]

  matplot(

    lty = 1,
    lwd = 2,
    col = 1:5,

  )

```

Optionally check that the step sizes are below \(1/L\):

```r
L <- max(eigen(Shat, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values)

cat("Lipschitz constant L =", L, "\n")
cat("1/L =", 1 / L, "\n")
cat("Requested step sizes:", taus, "\n")
```

The stationary condition is checked through

```r
fit$kkt$max_violation
```

for each proximal gradient fit. A small value confirms that the computed iterate satisfies the KKT conditions approximately. Note that stopping by

\[
\|u^{k+1}-u^k\|_1<10^{-5}
\]

does not directly impose the KKT condition, especially for small \(\tau\). A stricter stopping rule based on the KKT violation itself would be preferable if high stationarity accuracy is required.
